children.name: explore
children.instructions:
You are the EXPLORER. Do NOT implement the program. Build a VERIFIED behaviour specification of the reference program that a separate engineer will implement from. They will only have your spec, the docs and the reference.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.
1. Read every bundled documentation file. Capture the reference's own help output. Inventory every mode, flag (short and long), input source and output format.
2. Probe the reference systematically along every dimension below, for every mode. Use scripts so each tool call covers many inputs.
BEHAVIOUR DIMENSIONS (consider every one for every mode and feature):
1. Inputs: stdin; file arguments (one, several, missing, unreadable, `-`); network sources if documented (there is no internet: serve fixture files with `python3 -m http.server` on 127.0.0.1); every other argument form.
2. Outputs: exact stdout bytes, stderr, exit code; behaviour on empty input.
3. Flags: every flag listed by the program's help, in short AND long form, alone and in meaningful combinations; precedence when flags conflict.
4. Mode composition: feed each mode's OUTPUT into every other mode (round trips, chaining). Some modes only make sense on another mode's output; probing them with ordinary input is misleading.

children.name: build
children.instructions:
Implement the program FROM SCRATCH following spec/SPEC.md, and make `spec/run_cases.sh ./executable` pass 100%.
A pristine, execute-only copy of the reference program is at /opt/pb/reference/executable. It survives rebuilds (./compile.sh overwrites ./executable), so always compare against that path.
- Follow the task's build contract (./compile.sh producing ./executable), keep build artifacts out of git, and commit.
- Structure the code around the spec's modes and rules. Implement the GENERAL rules; never special-case individual case inputs.
- Run spec/run_cases.sh often. If you believe a case is wrong, re-run it against the reference: the reference is always right; re-capture with spec/capture.sh, never edit expected output by hand.
- Cover every dimension in the spec, including error paths and exit codes, environment, invocation name, terminal vs pipe, and large inputs.
